messages:
Sara Kim: Quick question — in the Create Dataset stepper: do we surface validation inline on blur or wait until submit? trying to avoid noisy red while still guiding users. Mike Chen: Inline on blur for short, single-line fields (email, name). gives fast feedback. For big freeform fields, validate on submit or explicit "check" to avoid interrupting flow. Ana Rodrigues: Agree on blur for atomic fields. Accessibility note: errors must be announced to screen readers. aria-live="polite" on the error container and move focus to the first invalid control on submit. Jason Patel: Related: required marker — keep the asterisk or use 'Required' label? asterisk alone isn't discoverable. Sara Kim: Proposal: keep visual asterisk, add visually-hidden "required" text for assistive tech. On small screens show an inline 'Required' under the label to avoid misses. Ana Rodrigues: Example snippet I would use: ```html
Name is required.
``` Mike Chen: design-bot flagged our error color (#d32f2f) — contrast fails for small text (3.8:1). Need an accessible tone that hits >=4.5:1. design-bot: automated check: error color contrast 3.8:1; recommended >=4.5 for body text. Jason Patel: For destructive flows (delete dataset) — typed confirm (type full name) vs checkbox + modal? typed confirm is highest safety but bad for quick ops. Sara Kim: Maybe tiered: typed confirm for org-level or shared datasets; simple modal + checkbox for user-level or small items. Ana Rodrigues: We can make it rule-driven: if dataset.size > 1GB OR sharedWithCount > 5 => require typed confirmation. Otherwise show modal with a mandatory "I understand" checkbox. Mike Chen: Also UI behavior: when submit fails server-side, keep form values intact and focus the first invalid field. show a concise inline message and a global top summary linking to fields. Sara Kim: Copy tone: keep it short and directive. e.g. 'Enter a valid email address.' rather than conversational. Designers okay with terse, microcopy-first approach? Ana Rodrigues: Yes — concise error strings improve scanability. avoid long explanations in the label. Jason Patel: Small accessibility nit: error icons should be decorative only (aria-hidden) unless they convey status beyond text. Otherwise provide an accessible name. Mike Chen: I'll mock two variants: 1) inline-on-blur with ARIA annotations, 2) submit-only with global summary and anchor links. will include contrast-adjusted colors and the typed-confirm rule examples. Sara Kim: Great — I'll add both flows to the Figma file and request an a11y pass. @Ana Rodrigues and @Jason Patel can you review after I upload? :thumbsup: Ana Rodrigues: Happy to review. Jason Patel: I'll take a look post-upload. Sara Kim: Thanks all — will post mock screenshots and copy options later today.
